beats.say: Hello! A file name can lie. Today we learn to see what an attachment really is.
This file looks like a PDF. But the very end of the name says exe, so it is a program.
Archives, disk images and shortcut files can also hide a program inside.
The rule is simple: check the type before opening an unexpected file, and report if in doubt.

scenes.title: Downloads folder
scenes.intro: Look at the files you downloaded from email. Show extensions and choose what to do with each.

steps.say: Show extensions. What does the end of the name say?

actions.label: Open
actions.feedback: This is not a document, it is a program. It can install malware the moment it opens.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Right. A real decree is never a program.

actions.label: Report to IT security
actions.feedback: Great. Security can remove the same email from everyone else's mailbox too.

actions.label: Open
actions.feedback: An ISO file opens like a disc and can hold a program. Reports are not sent as disk images.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Right. Do not open a disk image you did not expect.

actions.label: Report to IT security
actions.feedback: Great. An ISO posing as a report is a typical attack.

actions.label: Open
actions.feedback: It was a shortcut and it ran a hidden command. Photos are never 3 KB.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: Right. A shortcut (.lnk) posing as photos is a trap.

actions.label: Report to IT security
actions.feedback: Great. Reporting without opening is the safest way.

actions.label: Open
actions.feedback: Right. An expected PDF from an internal address is fine to open.

actions.label: Delete
actions.feedback: This file is safe: a real PDF from a known sender. Not every file needs deleting.

scenes.prompt: Find the warning signs in this email.

body.text: An administrative fine has been issued in your name. Details are attached.
If not paid within 3 days, the amount doubles.

spots.label: Fake domain
spots.explain: The address adds "-gov" and a different ending. Check the official portal domain yourself.

spots.label: Password protected archive
spots.explain: The password stops antivirus from looking inside. Official notices are not sent like this.

spots.label: HTML attachment
spots.explain: An HTML attachment opens a fake payment or sign-in page in the browser.

spots.label: Threat and rush
spots.explain: Fear is meant to make you open it without checking. Check fines only on the official portal.

cards.explain: Internal address, expected document, ordinary PDF. Fine to open.
A shortcut wearing a spreadsheet name. Opening it can run a hidden command.
IMG is a disk image. Order details are never sent this way.

source.text: Səbinə Kərimova, agreed for the meeting

cards.explain: An agreed presentation in a normal format. No warning signs.
Invoices are not HTML files. This one from a look-alike domain opens a sign-in page.

scenes.prompt: Match each file type to its risk.

pairs.right: A program that runs when opened
A shortcut that can run a hidden command
A disk image that can hide a program
Can open a fake sign-in page in the browser

scenes.explain: These types are rare in work email. If you did not expect one, do not open it and report it.

question.prompt: A colleague says: "I opened the file and nothing happened." What do you advise?

options.label: Disconnect from the network and call IT security right away
options.feedback: Right. Malware often runs silently, and reporting fast limits the damage.

options.label: Wait and report if something happens
options.feedback: "Nothing happened" is often a false impression. Waiting gives the attacker time.

options.label: Shut the computer down right away
options.feedback: Shutting down can erase evidence in memory. Unless your procedure says otherwise, leave it on, disconnect and report.

scenes.explain: An opened suspicious file is an incident: disconnect, keep the computer on, report at once.

points: Look at the very end of the name: the real type
Do not open unexpected archives, ISO, shortcuts or HTML
Opened it? Disconnect and report at once
